data.name: Khawaja
data.gender_notes: Khawaja is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'khadja' meaning 'to travel', 'Khawaja' is a title of respect given to a leader, a master, or a Sir. In Islamic history, 'Khawaja' is also used as a title for the spiritual guide of Sufi orders. The name Khawaja carries the meaning “Master, Sir, Leader” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khawaja usually hope their child will grow to embody master, sir, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual guide, a wise master leading you towards the truth.
data.etymology: Khawaja belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Master, Sir, Leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khawaja total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, 'Khawaja' signifies a spiritually enlightened master or a guide. In Sufi culture, a 'Khawaja' is a Sufi saint or a teacher of a Sufi order. Their wisdom, guidance, and spiritual practices serve as an inspiration and a source of strength for countless individuals throughout history and to the present day.
